findings.detail: The first SIGTERM raises SupervisorTerminated even when cleanup is already running. For example, if a command times out with a TERM-ignoring child, SIGTERM received while stop_group is observing that child interrupts the finally block before SIGKILL, reaping and final observations. The child runs in a separate session and can survive; final reconciliation only reports its group and cannot complete the skipped cleanup. Pipeline cleanup has the same unprotected interruption path.
findings.fix: Defer SIGTERM throughout command and pipeline cleanup, finish termination, reaping and diagnostic recording, then propagate the pending termination. Add coverage that delivers the first SIGTERM during cleanup.
findings.title: Uncited: SIGTERM can interrupt the cleanup it is meant to preserve.

findings.detail: Captured stdout, stderr and cleanup diagnostics are printed only after root_supervision exits successfully. If final reconciliation raises because a descendant remains unconfirmed, ps fails or the audit becomes unreadable, execution skips lines 21–24. The document's retained test output and original cleanup_error are then lost, leaving only the finalization traceback. This hides the diagnostics needed to explain the failed document.
findings.fix: Publish the captured streams and invalid-step diagnostics before leaving the supervision context, or from a finally block that also handles finalization failures. Report finalization errors separately and retain a nonzero exit.
findings.title: Uncited: Final supervision failures discard captured document diagnostics.

strengths: Cleanup preserves permission errors, subprocess diagnostics and phase expiration causes.
Missing parent allocations and unconfirmed process groups fail closed.
summary: Reviewed all membership paths for introduced error-handling problems, including supervision, publication, tests and documentation. Two Important issues remain; validation was static and no tests were run.
